subject: Post-call: Stakeholder map & next steps — identifying economic buyer and budget owner
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@brightwave.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Stakeholder map & next steps — identifying economic buyer and budget owner

Thanks again for taking time today, Marcus — really helpful conversation. I promised a concise recap with the suggested stakeholder map and the immediate next steps to move this forward. See the attached two-pager and MAP (mutual action plan).

Key points from today's call:
- Primary use case: reduce inference cost and improve 95th percentile latency for near-realtime recommendations across web + mobile.
- Current traffic / scale: ~80M tokens/day with daily peaks tied to promotions.
- Decision criteria you mentioned: 1) measurable latency gains, 2) no PII exfiltration risk, 3) predictable unit economics for planning.

Suggested stakeholder map (based on our conversation):
- Economic buyer / budget owner: Dana Ortiz (CFO) — final sign-off for infra spend and multi-year commitment
- Procurement: procurement@brightwave.com — contract and SOW negotiation
- Security / Legal: legal@brightwave.com — SOC2 and data residency questions
- Technical champion: Marcus Lin (you) — owns POC and success metrics

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Marcus — please confirm Dana's preferred intro channel (email intro vs calendar invite) and whether we should include procurement/legal on the first intro.
2) I'll prepare a one-page ROI summary tailored to Dana with topline cost savings and SLO guarantees (vailed to CFO audience).
3) Dev can stand up a scoped POC checklist; suggest a 4-week trial scoped to a single traffic shard.

If that aligns, I can draft the intro email to Dana and include the ROI one-pager and our MAP.

Attachments: post-call-stakeholder-map.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@brightwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Stakeholder map & next steps — identifying economic buyer and budget owner

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick clarifications:
- Confirmed: Dana Ortiz (CFO) is the budget owner and will need the business case.
- Procurement should be looped before contract talks but not on the very first intro; they prefer to see technical + commercial alignment first.
- Legal (legal@brightwave.com) will review data handling and SOC2 artifacts. They often want our standard data processing addendum early in the cycle.

Preferred intro: an email thread works best — Dana likes a brief 2–3 sentence summary and then the ask to schedule a 20–30 minute sync. If you can draft, I'll forward it to her with a short personal note.

One more: estimated budget band for this initiative is in the $150k–$300k ARR range for year 1 depending on commitment / dedicated capacity.

Happy to sync if you want to prep the CFO one-pager together — I can carve time Tues morning.

—Marcus
VP, Engineering (ML Platforms) | Brightwave Systems
marcus.lin@brightwave.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@brightwave.com>, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@brightwave.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@brightwave.com
Date: 2026-03-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Intro and one-pager: Redwood inference economics for Brightwave — Dana meet team

Hi Dana — Marcus suggested I reach out with a short summary and a proposed next step. Marcus — thanks for the quick confirmation of the budget range and procurement timing.

Dana — hi, pleasure to e-meet. I’m Marissa, AE at Redwood Inference. We help engineering orgs reduce per-token inference costs while improving tail latency through a mix of smart routing, prefix caching, and model quantization profiles.

Why this matters for Brightwave (TL;DR):
- Expected 20–35% reduction in per-token cost on similar workloads (benchmarks attached)
- Hold 95th percentile latency at or below your current SLOs with smaller footprint
- Predictable pricing paths for reserved capacity that map to annual budgeting cycles

If helpful, I’ve attached a one-page CFO-facing ROI summary and the stakeholder MAP. Would you be open to a 20-minute intro next week to review the topline numbers and procurement steps? Marcus suggested Tuesdays AM but we’re flexible.

Next actions proposed:
- Dana: confirm interest and preferred calendar windows; indicate if procurement/legal should be included in that first call.
- Marcus: if you’d like, add a short personal intro line in your forward to lend context.
- Dev: I’ve cc’d you — can you prepare a 1-paragraph POC scope that we can share pre-call?

Thanks — happy to adapt anything for Dana's preferred format.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: cfo-onepager-Brightwave.pdf, post-call-stakeholder-map.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Happy to help with the POC paragraph. Draft below — feel free to paste into the pre-call note or we can include it as a one-pager: 

POC scope (draft):
- Duration: 4 weeks, limited to the recommendations service (web recommendation model) for a single traffic shard (~5% of total traffic).
- Success metric: reduce per-token spend by >=20% while keeping 95th percentile latency within 10% of current baseline.
- Deliverables: deployment checklist, latency/cost dashboard access, weekly check-ins, final performance report.

I can join the intro call for 20 minutes to quickly walk the technical approach and POC assumptions.
